mission: Desh gives the escapee a name - Veraine - and the ship reorganizes itself around the fact that the enemy is a specific person already ahead of them.
why_now: The monitoring packets finished overnight per Ch 5 s4 setup. The first hour of this transit leg is when Desh brings the name to Ben — and the reveal reframes the entire mission from 'pursue an anchor' to 'pursue Darth Veraine, specifically.'
conflict: The name lands and the room reorganises around it. Sera's composure holds; her knowledge of Veraine is obvious and unoffered. Torin's warmth momentarily thins and restores itself. Kael's reaction — recognition, then studied blankness — is the load-bearing small beat Ben notices and files. Later in the scene, Sera tests Ben with a tactical question about the Corridor route; his pragmatic answer earns the first grudging respect.
turning_point: Desh names Veraine. The escapee's shape acquires a signature: Brotherhood alchemist, strategist, patient. Ben now has the antagonist the story has been withholding since s3 of the prior chapter. The mission's forward vector sharpens.
opening_hook: Desh finds Ben in the cramped common area at first watch — datapad in hand, the reconstructed monitoring packets resolved. 'We have a name,' Desh says. Ben looks up. Sera, across the table, does not
closing_hook: Torin finds Ben alone in the corridor after the briefing and says something warm about Luke — 'Your father's name carries weight even in our time.' The compliment feels genuine. It also feels, very faintly, like an assessment
emotional_trajectory: Reveal absorption -> tension and territorial friction -> unexpected competence demonstration -> uneasy truce

stakes.personal: Ben is now pursuing Darth Veraine by name, a Brotherhood-era Sith whose capability Sera will not articulate out loud
stakes.interpersonal: The group's ability to function — fracture here means failure everywhere; Kael's reaction to the name seeds the Veraine/Kael channel the book will open at Ch 10
stakes.external: Every moment of internal friction is time Veraine is using to get further ahead along the Corridor

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns in hyperspace — cramped common area, corridor, cockpit
sensory_details: The ship straining with extra passengers; Sera's hand closing on blank hull plating where a console used to be; Torin's ease in small spaces and the old-soldier instinct of standing where he will not block a door; Kael folded into a corner, watching; the reconstructed monitoring file open on the table, Veraine's name visible in the header
canon_elements_needed: Sith alchemy in Legends EU tradition and capabilities
Brotherhood of Darkness era Sith training and specializations
Darth title usage and Sith identity in the Brotherhood era
action_beats: Desh presents the reconstructed monitoring file to the group; Veraine's name is the first clean line in the display
Sera's composure holds; the silence after the name is hers and she does not fill it with explanation
Kael's reaction to the name — recognition, then studied blankness — is the scene's quietest and most important beat; Ben registers and files it
Torin makes a small, warm remark that restores the room, without diminishing the weight of the name
Sera reaches for a cockpit control that doesn't exist on a modern ship — her hand closing on blank hull plating
Sera tests Ben with a tactical question about the Corridor route; his pragmatic answer earns her posture's first half-degree shift
Torin clasps Ben's shoulder in the corridor — a commander's measured grip of acknowledgment that lands as both approval and assessment
promises_planted: Veraine's philosophy will be coherent and unsettling (PP16)
Mere tactical cooperation won't work; the climax demands genuine unity (PP23)
notes: Kael's reaction is the quiet center. Let the room shift around the name without turning the scene into a history lesson.
